subject: Hosted API commit settlement & quarterly reconciliation process

Subject: Clarify commit true-ups + make-good options for Hosted API

Hi Neha,

Quick question as we finalize internal budget: how does Redwood handle quarterly/annual true-ups against hosted API per-token commit tiers? Specifically:
- If we commit to a quarterly token volume and underuse, is there an option to credit future quarters vs. an invoice charge?
- If we overuse, what’s the standard overage rate and are make-goods applied as credits or invoices after the quarter closes?
- Any minimums for rollovers or caps on credits?

We’re also looking at a blended discount structure across 3 tiers and want to understand the settlement mechanics so we can model cashflow. Happy to hop on a short call — Aisha and I are on PT.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Fwd: Draft guidance + workbook for Nimbus commit settlement

Neha — draft language and workbook attached. Key points summarized below (feel free to copy into the reply to Samir):

1) Commit tiers & discounts (hosted API, per-token):
   - Tier A: 0–500M tokens / mo => list price (no commit discount)
   - Tier B: 500M–2B tokens / mo => 12% discount off list
   - Tier C: 2B+ tokens / mo => 20% discount off list
   - Discounts apply to actual tokens consumed within the billing period once true-up is applied.

2) Quarterly true-up mechanics (recommended default):
   - At the end of each quarter we compare committed tokens (sum of three months) to actual consumption.
   - If consumption >= commit: customer pays the committed buckets at discounted rates; any overage above committed tokens billed at the agreed overage rate (list price minus 5% adder) and appears on the quarter-end invoice.
   - If consumption < commit: customer has two options (specified in SOW):
       a) Elect credit: unused committed token value converted into account credits valid for 2 future quarters (no cash refund).
       b) Elect make-good invoice: Redwood issues an invoice for the shortfall at the committed discounted rate (standard for enterprise finance teams that prefer no credits).

3) Make-goods / credits:
   - Credits expire after 2 quarters; partial-quarter prorations supported.
   - No retroactive increase in discount band from credits alone (discount band for a quarter determined by that quarter’s committed tier).

4) Overage pricing:
   - Default overage = list price * 1.0 (no discount) unless previously negotiated; for committed customers we recommend list price minus 5% adder for predictability.

5) Reporting & audit:
   - Redwood will provide token-level monthly reports and a quarter consolidation file used for reconciliation.

Attachment: Proposed_Commit_Tiers_v3.xlsx (worked examples: under/over scenarios, cashflow impact, sample invoice lines).

Notes for Neha: Ben suggests we leave the credit vs invoice election as a customer-selectable clause in the SOW to accommodate Nimbus’ finance preference.

-Ben

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-07T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft guidance + workbook for Nimbus commit settlement

Adding finance perspective and the preferred default for enterprise deals:

- Accounting treatment: credits are preferred operationally (reduces invoice churn) but we must track deferred revenue appropriately when credits are granted; legal/finance needs clear SOW language if credits are used.
- Make-good invoice flow: if Nimbus elects make-good invoice, invoice is generated within 10 business days after quarter close and is due on the normal invoice terms.
- Rollover constraints: credits that originate from a quarterly shortfall may only be applied to future Hosted API usage (cannot be used for Dedicated or Private fees).
- Minimums: we recommend a contract clause that prevents rolling forward credits that would drop a future quarter below a minimum billing floor (e.g., $5k/mo equivalent) to avoid perpetual low-usage churn.
- Edge cases: if customer under-commits and then has an unexpected spike that pushes them to a higher discount band retroactively, discount band is only applied going forward (no retroactive rebate on previously billed quarters).

I attached sample T&Cs for make-goods (Sample_MakeGood_T&Cs.pdf). If they want cash refunds instead of credits we’ll need exec approval and finance will scope the levers (typically only granted in limited cases).

—Vivek

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple follow-ups so we can model: 
1) Example: If we commit to 1.5B tokens for Q1 and consume 1.2B, what is the credit calculation? Is it the dollar value of 300M tokens at the committed discounted rate?
2) If we under-commit in Q1 but then in Q2 consume 3B (moving into Tier C), can any credits from Q1 be used to offset the Q2 liability immediately or do they apply only to future months of Q2?
3) For overage invoices, what are the typical SLA windows — what date will the overage invoice appear and how quickly do you expect payment?

Also, can you confirm that credits are applied on a FIFO basis against future monthly usage and that they will appear as a line item on the month they’re consumed?

If you have a one-page flow diagram, that would be ideal for our procurement team. Otherwise we’re happy to use the workbook and a short call.

Samir

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit settlement & quarterly reconciliation process

Samir — answered inline and attached a quick one-page flow. See also the workbook examples.

1) Credit calc: correct — the unused 300M tokens are converted into a credit equal to the dollar value at the committed discounted rate (e.g., Tier B rate). The workbook shows the math and invoice lines.
2) Credit usage timing: credits created at Q1 reconciliation are available immediately at the start of Q2; they apply FIFO against each month’s consumption in Q2 until exhausted. They can be used in Q2 even if Q2 pushes you into Tier C, but credits themselves do not re-trigger retroactive discounting for prior quarters.
3) Overage invoice timing: overage invoices are issued within 10 business days after quarter close; standard payment terms apply (Net 30 by default). For committed customers we can coordinate custom terms in the SOW.

Next steps: I’ll send the one-pager and the two attachments (Proposed_Commit_Tiers_v3.xlsx, Sample_MakeGood_T&Cs.pdf) now and schedule a 20m call for next week to walk through the workbook with Nimbus procurement if that helps.
